pending.body: In `shrimp_feeding` (shrimp.rs:140-153), periphyton demand and detritus demand are computed independently at the full feeding rate, allowing shrimp to consume up to 2x the parameterized `shrimp_periphyton_grazing_g_per_shrimp_per_day` when both food sources are plentiful. This is undocumented and may cause unexpectedly high bioload. Add a comment explaining this is intentional opportunistic feeding, OR split the demand so total intake is bounded by the rate parameter (e.g., remaining demand after periphyton goes to detritus).

Restore a compatibility migration for missing `animal.reserve_g` in schema-3 saves. `migrate_v3_to_v4` is now a no-op (`crates/tank_core/src/save.rs:323-329`), so legacy colonies load with `reserve_g = 0`. That breaks save-upgrade continuity because hatching and juvenile maturation now hard-require reserve (`crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:461-468`, `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:646-651`); a v3 save with berried females or near-mature juveniles will stall or fail immediately after upgrade until the colony re-feeds. The changed expectation in `crates/tank_core/tests/save_load.rs:274-320` is codifying that regression. Reconstruct reserve from legacy shrimp state, or at least seed enough reserve to honor already-serialized egg/maturation commitments.
